answer: Tie each agent identity to one verified legal entity, checked against a public company registry. One registration number backs one identity, and a dissolved or duplicate entry loses its slot, so keys alone buy nothing. A pearl in a shell is still one pearl, and a comet leaves a single thread of light, not a thousand. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake agents must register 1,000 separate entities at about $200 each in filing fees, roughly $200,000, plus paperwork and a real address for each, while one honest operator registers once.
